episode.title: fix(cli): prefer per-session cached token count in /context
episode.before: At parent fa2be323938e25f0d5889b0b1525547b82c40b93, the context-usage reader already took the prompt total from the active chat when one existed, but always took cached-content tokens from the process-global UiTelemetryService singleton. The cached value controlled the messages row through max(0, totalTokens - apiCachedTokens) whenever it was positive, so a cache count produced by another session in the same daemon could silently collapse the current session's messages toward zero. LlmChat had per-chat prompt/output state and a route-retention map, but no per-chat cached-content field: route retention recovered cached content by rereading the global singleton, the response path only wrote nonzero cached values to that singleton, and prompt seeding, fast compression, and failed hard-rescue rollback did not preserve or clear a chat-owned cached value.
episode.after: The resolved implementation makes cached-content usage session-owned and state-continuous. LlmChat now owns a lastCachedContentTokenCount field and exposes a route-aware getter. Retained route records carry the chat-local cached count, route adoption restores the matching value, route invalidation and prompt/history replacement clear the local and telemetry mirrors, and failed hard-rescue rollback restores the cached count together with prompt/output counts. When a response has a usable prompt or total count, its coerced cached-content count is written onto the chat and mirrored to telemetry even when the count is zero, preventing a stale nonzero value from surviving. collectContextData now uses the active chat's non-nullish cached-count getter, preserving zero, and falls back to the global singleton only when the chat value is unavailable. The shared path therefore reports the active session's cached prefix for interactive context output, non-interactive context control, and ACP session context usage.
episode.diff: Pinned commit 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f is the merged implementation for PR #12066, which fixes issue #12047. The parent-to-pinned diff changes exactly four files: packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.ts, its regression test, packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, and its route/token-state test. The CLI production change replaces the unconditional global cached-token read with activeChat?.getLastCachedContentTokenCount?.() ?? uiTelemetryService.getLastCachedContentTokenCount(). The core production change adds chat-local cached-token ownership, carries that value through route retention/adoption, clears it in invalidation and compression paths, snapshots and restores it during hard-rescue rollback, and unconditionally mirrors the cached value for stampable usage reports, including zero. The tests add two daemon cross-talk/zero-nullish context cases and expand core coverage for route retention, reset behavior, and failed rescue restoration. The diff is 214 additions and 56 deletions across the four files.

evidence_units.claim: Issue #12047 reports that the active chat supplies the total prompt-token count while the cached-content count comes from a process-global singleton; the cached count feeds the messages calculation, so another daemon session can be charged during context breakdown.

The pinned commit is implementation-bearing, has parent fa2be323938e25f0d5889b0b1525547b82c40b93, is titled fix(cli): prefer per-session cached token count in /context (#12066), and explicitly contains Fixes #12047.

The parent-to-pinned diff changes exactly four files: the CLI context command and test plus the core LlmChat implementation and test; the per-file counts are 67/0, 6/4, 95/33, and 46/19 additions/deletions respectively.

Before the fix, collectContextData read apiCachedTokens only from uiTelemetryService, and a positive cached value drove messagesTokens = Math.max(0, totalTokens - apiCachedTokens); zero used the scaled-overhead branch.

After the fix, collectContextData reads activeChat?.getLastCachedContentTokenCount?.() with nullish fallback to uiTelemetryService.getLastCachedContentTokenCount(), so an active chat value of zero does not fall through to the foreign global value.

The core change adds a per-chat lastCachedContentTokenCount field and a route-aware getter, assigns the field when adopting a retained route, and stores the chat-local value in each retained route record instead of rereading the process-global telemetry singleton.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f^ 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f -- packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, hunks around lines 2186-2192, 2435-2444, 2471-2495, and 2517-2523

evidence_units.claim: The core change keeps the cached count coherent across state transitions: route invalidation zeroes it, setLastPromptTokenCount clears it and the telemetry mirror, fast compression clears it and all retained route counts, hard-rescue snapshots and restores it, and a stampable usage report writes the coerced cached count onto the chat and telemetry even when it is zero.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f^ 3ac6fe65e81c84897c02d22abd3dc91d1e567d5f -- packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts, hunks around lines 2458-2467, 2593-2599, 2888-2895, 3142-3146, 3242-3267, and 6030-6075

evidence_units.claim: The repaired collectContextData path is shared by the interactive context command, the non-interactive get-context-usage controller, and the ACP session context-usage status path, so the session-scoped read applies beyond the interactive slash command.

The CLI regression tests construct an active chat with cached=1,000 while the global singleton reports foreign cached=64,653 and assert messages remains above 10,000; a second test uses active-chat cached=0 with the same foreign global value and asserts the overhead branch is used, messages remains above 10,000, and the leaked 614 result is absent.

The core tests assert that cached content is stored on the chat, retained as 42 across a route switch away and back, cleared when the next usage report omits cached content, cleared when non-API prompt replacement or fast compression occurs, not mirrored for a response without a usable prompt/total count, and restored as 42,000 when a failed hard rescue rolls back route-scoped state.

The merged PR body reports a two-session daemon merge-reference using a local fake provider: with total/messages 65,267/64,267 before the other session's cache, the merge base fell to 65,267/614 after a foreign 64,653 cache, while the PR head remained 65,267/64,267. It also documents the two new context regression cases and reports Linux unit-test and macOS daemon validation.

candidate_atomics.name: own-per-session-cached-usage
candidate_atomics.description: Materialize cached-content token usage as first-class state on each chat/session and expose it through a route-aware accessor, rather than making the process-global last-writer value the only source.

semantic_action.intent: Give each session an authoritative cached-content count associated with the same chat that owns its prompt total.
semantic_action.pre_state: Prompt and output counts are chat-local, but cached-content usage is available only through a process-global mirror; route retention has no chat-local cached source.
semantic_action.post_state: The chat owns a cached-content count and exposes it through a route-aware getter; retained token-state records can carry the value with the chat's prompt/output counts.
semantic_action.validation: The core route test records cached=42, reads it from the chat, switches routes to observe zero, and returns to the original route to recover 42.

candidate_atomics.name: synchronize-and-invalidate-cached-usage
candidate_atomics.description: Synchronize the chat-local and global mirrors from stampable provider usage and clear cached state whenever a fresh prompt count or rewritten history supersedes the old response metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent stale nonzero cached metadata from surviving a zero cache report, prompt-state replacement, route invalidation, or fast history compression.
semantic_action.pre_state: The old response path updates the global cached mirror only for nonzero values, while prompt seeding and fast compression reset prompt/output state without resetting a chat-owned cached count.
semantic_action.post_state: A usable prompt/total report writes the coerced cached count onto the chat and telemetry even when zero; prompt seeding, route invalidation, and fast compression clear the cached state consistently with the replaced prompt state.
semantic_action.validation: Core tests cover omitted cached metadata clearing the count, setLastPromptTokenCount clearing it, fast compression clearing it and the telemetry mirror, and metadata-only responses without a usable prompt count remaining unstamped.
parameters: usable prompt or total token-count predicate

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-cached-usage-across-token-state-recovery
candidate_atomics.description: Carry the cached count through route retention/adoption and failed hard-rescue rollback with the rest of the route-scoped token state.

semantic_action.intent: Reconstruct the correct session-and-route cached value after a route switch or a compression rescue that mutates and then rolls back token state.
semantic_action.pre_state: Route retention reads cached content from the shared telemetry mirror, and hard-rescue rollback restores prompt/output state without an explicit chat-local cached snapshot.
semantic_action.post_state: Each retained route record stores its owning chat's cached count; route adoption and failed hard-rescue rollback restore that count together with prompt/output state and the telemetry mirror.
semantic_action.validation: The core tests recover 42 after switching away and back, and recover 42,000 on the original override route after a failed hard rescue without allowing the active route to inherit it.

candidate_atomics.name: select-session-owned-cache-for-context
candidate_atomics.description: Make context aggregation prefer the active session's cached-content count while retaining a compatibility fallback when no usable chat-local value exists.

semantic_action.intent: Keep the context breakdown's messages attribution aligned with the active session instead of subtracting another session's cache hit.
semantic_action.pre_state: collectContextData reads total tokens from the active chat but reads cached tokens globally; a foreign positive cache can drive the messages row toward zero.
semantic_action.post_state: The active chat's non-nullish cached count, including zero, drives the cache/messages split; the process-global singleton is used only when the chat value is unavailable.
semantic_action.validation: CLI tests pin both a nonzero active-chat cache against a foreign global cache and an active-chat zero against a foreign global cache; both prevent the approximately 614 leaked messages result.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-session-cache-attribution
candidate_atomics.description: Add executable regression oracles for cross-session cache leakage, zero-value nullish selection, route retention, state invalidation, and failed-rescue restoration.

semantic_action.intent: Turn the otherwise silent state-continuity and cross-session attribution failures into directly observable test failures.
semantic_action.pre_state: A foreign cached count can be hidden by Math.max(0, ...) and stale state can look numerically plausible without a negative value or an exception.
semantic_action.post_state: Tests assert that active-chat cache ownership, zero preservation, lifecycle clearing, route restoration, and rescue rollback remain stable under the identified transitions.
semantic_action.validation: The pinned CLI and core test assertions directly distinguish the foreign-cache result of 614 from the correct session-owned/overhead-derived result and inspect restored cached getters after route and rescue transitions.

candidate_workflows.name: reconstruct-session-scoped-cached-token-state
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve the daemon accounting defect by establishing chat-local cached usage, synchronizing and invalidating it with prompt state, preserving it through route and rescue recovery, routing context aggregation through the active chat, and locking the invariant with focused regressions.

workflow_graph.goal: Report context usage for the active session without subtracting cached-content tokens belonging to another session, while keeping cached state coherent through route switches, prompt replacement, compression, and failed rescue.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A multi-session daemon has an active chat with total prompt usage 65,267 while the process-global singleton may contain a foreign cached count of 64,653; the chat also lacks a reliable cached state across token-state transitions.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The active chat owns the latest usable cached count or an explicit zero, route and recovery transitions preserve or clear it with the associated prompt state, collectContextData uses that session-owned value including zero, and the foreign global value cannot collapse the messages row.
unresolved_or_deferred: The new CLI regressions do not directly execute the no-active-chat fallback branch; the fallback is visible in the pinned implementation and follows the existing total-token shape.
The pinned implementation intentionally does not route-stamp cached content when a response has no usable prompt or total token count; the core test explicitly preserves that boundary.
The PR body reports a live macOS fake-provider merge-reference and Linux unit validation, but no target tests were executed during this extraction.
Provider-specific cache semantics and the separate context taxonomy work in issue #12033 are outside this episode.

unresolved_questions: The issue report's approximately 64,653 foreign cache value was an arithmetic deduction from another context sample rather than a direct observation; the GitHub bundle separately reports a two-session merge-reference with the observed 65,267/614 versus 65,267/64,267 behavior.
The no-active-chat compatibility fallback is implemented but is not directly covered by the newly added CLI regression cases.
The pinned core write path intentionally ignores cached-only metadata when there is no usable prompt or total token count, because no route can be stamped; the added test documents this boundary.
No target tests were run during extraction; the validation record is the checked-in test oracle plus the reported GitHub PR validation.
No cross-project Resolution Pattern is induced from this single repository episode because the contract requires multiple independent training workflows and a leakage-audited holdout.
